subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw core expose a shell-facing admin notification broadcast for connected Control UI clients, and what auth scope, targeting, payload, delivery, and abuse-control contract should it use?
rationale: Current main has adjacent pieces but no canonical notification event; choosing the permanent admin/UI contract affects stable Gateway APIs and security boundaries.

options.title: Define a narrow core notify contract
options.body: Add a small admin-only CLI/Gateway/UI notification path with typed payloads, explicit target semantics, limits, docs, and tests while leaving cron/context workflows to #20237.

options.title: Fold into #20237
options.body: Keep this issue linked as a subproblem of the broader WebUI notification architecture and implement the shell command only after the shared toast/event model is approved.

options.title: Defer outside core
options.body: Do not add a core command now; require plugins or hooks to use existing Web Push and Gateway APIs until a missing extension API is identified.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core notify contract
recommendation.body: Add a small admin-only CLI/Gateway/UI notification path with typed payloads, explicit target semantics, limits, docs, and tests while leaving cron/context workflows to #20237.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice centers on the CLI/Gateway admin event contract and broadcast/security behavior where steipete has the strongest recent provenance.
